title: The Answering Light
hook: The lighthouse logbook had one rule: if a light ever flashes back at you from the water, do not answer it.
lines: I took a winter job keeping an old lighthouse. The logbook had one rule, on the very first page.
Keep the lamp turning. And if a light ever flashes back at you from the water... do not answer it.
No boats come out in winter. It was just me, the wind, and the beam going round and round.
On my ninth night, far past the rocks, a small light started blinking. Three short. Three long. Three short.
I grabbed the signal lamp and aimed it at the water. My thumb was already on the switch.
Then I flipped back through the logbook, looking for the coast guard's number.
Every keeper before me had an entry for their ninth night. All of them said the same thing.
Light on the water. Not answered.
Every keeper... except the last one. His entry was just one word. Answered.
Underneath, in shaky pencil: Someone is rowing in.
There's nothing after that. Not one page. Until tonight.
I haven't written a word tonight. But tonight's page is already filled in... in my handwriting.
